comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C3, C21-C23, C26, C30-C31 regarding comprehensive matrisome identification and classification. Both evaluations find the methodology thorough and the findings well-supported by computational and experimental approaches.

Perfect agreement on claims C4-C5, C37-C40, C107 regarding cell-type-specific expression and gastrodermal localization. Both evaluations praise the integration of scRNA-Seq data with matrisome analysis and support the mesoderm homology interpretation.

Perfect agreement on claims C54-C64 regarding cnidocyte-specific ECM characterization through scRNA-Seq analysis. Both evaluations support the comprehensive identification of cell types expressing matrisome components, with no concerns raised about the findings.

Perfect agreement on claims C32-C36 regarding structural characterization using immunofluorescence and electron microscopy. Both evaluations support the multi-method approach and find the structural findings well-documented.

Strong agreement on claims C10-C11, C94-C96, C100-C101 regarding elastic fiber components and developmental transitions. Both evaluations support the proteomic findings, though OpenEval notes functional inferences are reasonable but not directly tested, while peer review raises no such concerns.

Strong agreement on claims C42-C43, C46-C50 regarding collagen identification and characterization. Both evaluations support the domain analysis and expression data. Peer review also includes C51 and C53 (spongin-like proteins) which OpenEval addresses separately in R15.

Strong agreement on claims C6-C8, C67, C70-C72 regarding Polydom family expansion and epithelial remodeling during larva-to-polyp transition. Peer review also includes C9, C84, C92 (Wnt/PCP components) which OpenEval addresses separately in R4, but both find the developmental findings convincing.

Partial overlap on claims C9, C84, C92 regarding Wnt/PCP component enrichment. OpenEval finds these supported but notes lack of direct functional validation in Nematostella, while peer review groups these with broader developmental findings and expresses no concerns.

Agreement on claims C77-C79 regarding Polydom family identification and expression. OpenEval notes the genetic robustness inference (C79) is speculative, while peer review finds the overall characterization convincing. Peer review also includes C81-C83 (sIntREP functional hypotheses) which OpenEval addresses separately in R13.

Divergent evaluation on claims C81, C83 regarding sIntREP functional hypotheses. OpenEval rates these as UNCERTAIN due to lack of functional validation in Nematostella, explicitly noting they are speculative. Peer review rates the broader group (including these claims) as SUPPORTED, finding the hypotheses plausible within the comprehensive analysis.

Agreement on claims C113-C115 regarding comparative matrisome sizes across cnidarian species. Both evaluations support the evolutionary analysis, though OpenEval notes the interpretation is somewhat speculative. Peer review emphasizes the work's value for understanding matrisome evolution.

Agreement on claims C24-C25 comparing Nematostella findings with previous Hydra study. Both evaluations support the comparative analysis showing greater compositional diversity. Peer review groups this with broader evolutionary claims (C28-C29, C113-C115).

Agreement on claims C28-C29 regarding differential expansion patterns between core and associated matrisome components. Both evaluations support the comparative analysis. Peer review groups this with broader evolutionary findings.

Agreement on claims C98-C99 regarding protease/inhibitor balance. OpenEval finds these supported by quantitative proteomics, and peer review includes these within broader developmental findings that are praised as thorough.

Agreement on claims C51-C53 regarding spongin-like proteins and minicollagens. OpenEval supports these based on domain analysis and expression data, while peer review includes these within the comprehensive collagen characterization effort.

OpenEval finds claims C68-C69 (vitellogenin identification and function) supported by quantitative proteomics. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found, though these findings would fall within the overall praised proteomic analysis.

OpenEval finds claim C93 (lack of fibrillar collagen upregulation during larva-to-polyp transition) supported by proteomic data. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found, though this would be part of the developmental analysis praised by reviewers.

OpenEval rates claims C109-C110, C117, C127, C129-C130 as UNCERTAIN, noting these are explicitly speculative hypotheses without direct experimental validation. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found addressing these speculative claims.

Peer review raises methodological concern about claims C23, C66 regarding potential underestimation of collagen abundance due to omission of certain post-translational modifications in proteomic analysis. OpenEval does not specifically address this methodological limitation, instead grouping C23 with other supported matrisome identification claims in R1.

Peer review explicitly supports background/contextual claims C1-C2, C12-C15, C102, C105 as established facts that frame the study's importance. OpenEval does not evaluate these background claims, focusing instead on novel findings from the study.
